chunks: Say: 'Just think. If this is from God and you deny it, who will be in greater error than he who is in open dissent?'

key_terms.أَضَلُ: more astray or in greater error

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about those who deny it if it is from God?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the logical inevitability of faith when the Quran is recognized as divine revelation, contrasting the disbelievers' stubborn rejection with mere disagreement. It highlights that denial after acknowledging the source constitutes a deeper spiritual misguidance, a theme often linked to the concept of *'Ilm al-Yaqin* (knowledge of certainty) preceding *'Ayn al-Yaqin* (eye of certainty). This reinforces the Shia emphasis on the Quran's internal coherence as proof of its divine origin, making rejection a conscious choice against evident truth.
